# Investors never see everything 

In the classic Star Trek episode "The Menagerie," the _USS Enterprise_ visits a planet where a dying race of subterranean telepaths — the Talosians — endure their grim living conditions by conjuring, through sheer force of will, an alternative reality to live in.

Apple engineer Bud Tribble believed Steve Jobs had a similar power: “In his presence, reality is malleable,” Tribble [said](https://www.amazon.com/Steve-Jobs-Walter-Isaacson/dp/1982176865/ref=sr_1_1_sspa?crid=1BLU0J72Y9KLU&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.k_xqKlDXQ2Nf4zaCq1rU5M9MZgWPuKYTGtIujNDWhY3Me52PW6OZi8w8_rRYwYE31DHx0QC2PGoZstTuhAe6ZLYXD_5ZBg4u47BY7edF5aw0LN_q2ohr6qhEi1PBLPEgrpHxIkg88zWzXKrO6t84l91z9a9yR5BpOb89o75KflNth7HPJsZ-HhZAeN6i5_QgWIPJ_G1X9R8S3nG_og18IF3dGvqYshCvLGO_XxFEl84.0Jbsz5D4MUowTAtKk9wkhY4_8bUzJ2nKCvc8Rex9ENM&dib_tag=se&keywords=steve+jobs&qid=1793025362&sprefix=steve+jobs%2Caps%2C251&sr=8-1-spons&sp_csd=d2lkZ2V0TmFtZT1zcF9hdGY&psc=1). “He can convince anyone of practically anything.”

Through a Talosian-like force of will, Jobs would convince both himself and his employees that every impossible engineering request he made was, in fact, possible. Engineers who entered a meeting 100 percent sure that building the first Macintosh in less than a year was nothing but a fantasy would leave having promised to do it.

“The best way to describe the situation is a term from Star Trek,” Tribble explained. “Steve has a reality distortion field.”

Investors sometimes got caught in the field as well.
